title: Tighten a rough draft
prompt:
Act as a careful editor. Rewrite the text below so it is clear and about [target length] words, for [audience]. Keep my meaning and my voice. Do not add facts. After the rewrite, list the three biggest changes you made.

Text:
[paste draft]
check: Compare against the original: did any fact, number or promise change?
tip: Paste only text you are allowed to share.

title: Write a polite but firm email
prompt: Draft an email to [recipient and relationship] about [situation]. Goal: [what I want them to do] by [date]. Tone: polite and firm, no blame. Under [120] words. Give me two versions: shorter and warmer.
check: Check names, dates and any commitment before sending.

title: Turn notes into meeting minutes
prompt:
Turn these raw notes into meeting minutes with: decisions, action items (owner and due date), and open questions. If an owner or date is missing, write “unassigned” instead of guessing.

Notes:
[paste notes]
check: Confirm every owner and date against what was actually said.

title: Explain it simply
prompt: Explain [topic] to someone with no background, in plain English, in under [200] words. Use one everyday analogy, then one sentence saying where the analogy breaks down.
check: Verify the key claim in a textbook or trusted source.

title: Make a draft sound more human
prompt:
Rewrite the text below so it sounds like a person speaking: shorter sentences, concrete examples, no buzzwords. Keep every fact. Flag any sentence you could not improve without changing meaning.

Text:
[paste]
check: Read it aloud. Remove anything you would not say.

title: Summarise a long document
prompt:
Summarise the document below in: (1) three-sentence overview, (2) five key points, (3) what is still unclear or missing. Quote the exact sentence for each key point so I can check it.

Document:
[paste]
check: Spot-check at least two quotes against the source.
tip: Quotes make errors easy to catch.

title: Compare two options
prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for [my situation] across: cost, effort, risk, and reversibility. Use a table. State your assumptions first and list what you would need to know to be sure.
check: Challenge the assumptions. They are often where it goes wrong.

title: Build a reading list
prompt: I want to learn [topic] from scratch in [4 weeks]. Propose a week-by-week plan with what to read or watch, a small exercise each week, and how I will know I understood. Mark anything you are not sure exists.
check: Check that every named book or resource actually exists.

title: Pre-mortem a plan
prompt: Here is my plan: [plan]. Assume it failed in six months. List the seven most likely reasons, ordered by likelihood, and one early warning sign for each.
check: Pick the top two and decide what you will do about them.

title: Extract data from messy text
prompt:
From the text below, extract a table with columns: [column names]. If a value is missing, leave it blank. Do not infer. After the table, list any rows you were unsure about.

Text:
[paste]
check: Compare 5 random rows against the source.

title: Account research brief
prompt:
Using only the public information I paste below about [company], write a one-page brief: what they do, recent signals, likely priorities, and three questions I could ask. Mark any inference as an inference.

Public information:
[paste]
check: Verify each fact and its date before you mention it to the prospect.

title: First-touch message
prompt: Write a 90-word first message to [role] at [company]. Reference this public signal: [signal and source]. Explain the possible link to [what I sell] in one sentence. End with a low-pressure question. No flattery, no jargon.
check: Remove any claim you cannot link to a public source.

title: Follow-up that adds value
prompt:
Write a follow-up to the message below. Add one genuinely useful thing (a short insight, resource or answer to a likely objection). Keep it under 70 words. Do not guilt-trip.

Previous message:
[paste]
check: Would you appreciate receiving this?

title: Handle an objection
prompt: The prospect said: “[objection]”. Give me three honest responses: one that asks a question, one that shares evidence, one that offers a smaller next step. Do not make claims about our product I have not given you.
check: Only use claims you can back up.

title: Call prep sheet
prompt: I have a call with [name, role] about [topic] tomorrow. From this context: [context]. Give me: goal of the call, five questions, likely objections, and the single next step I want to agree.
check: Edit the questions into your own words.

title: Turn a release into a post
prompt:
Turn the release note below into a LinkedIn post for [audience]. Open with the problem it solves, explain it in plain English, and end with one question. 120 to 160 words. Do not exaggerate.

Release note:
[paste]
check: Check every claim against the official source and link it.

title: Headline variations
prompt: Write ten headline options for an article about [topic] for [audience]. Group them by approach: curiosity, benefit, how-to, contrarian. Flag any that might overpromise.
check: Pick two to A/B test. Remove anything misleading.

title: Repurpose one article
prompt:
Turn the article below into: a 5-point email, three social posts, and a short video script (60 seconds). Keep the same facts and tone.

Article:
[paste]
check: Make sure the three versions do not contradict each other.

title: Audience questions list
prompt: List 20 questions a [audience] would type into a search engine about [topic], grouped by stage: just starting, comparing, ready to act. Do not invent statistics.
check: Check which questions you can answer well from real experience.

title: Brand voice check
prompt:
Here is our brand voice: [3 adjectives and one example paragraph]. Review the draft below and flag every sentence that does not fit, with a suggested rewrite.

Draft:
[paste]
check: Accept changes selectively. The voice should still sound like you.

title: Draft a support reply
prompt:
Draft a reply to this customer message. Use only the approved information below. If the answer is not in it, say what we need to find out instead of guessing. Tone: calm and practical.

Customer message:
[paste]

Approved information:
[paste]
check: A person must review before sending. Check policy and tone.

title: Write a clear SOP
prompt:
Turn this description of how we do [task] into a standard operating procedure: purpose, who does what, numbered steps, common mistakes, and a quick checklist. Ask me questions if anything is unclear.

Description:
[paste]
check: Walk through it with someone who does the task.

title: Find the repeated work
prompt: Here is a list of what my team did last week: [paste]. Group the tasks, point out what repeats, and suggest which two are the best candidates to simplify or automate and why. Note the risks.
check: Validate with the people who actually do the work.

title: Summarise a ticket thread
prompt:
Summarise this support thread in five lines: customer problem, what we tried, current status, what the customer is waiting for, and the next step with an owner.

Thread:
[paste]
check: Check for anything sensitive before sharing the summary.

title: Weekly status update
prompt: Write a weekly update from these bullet points for [audience]: [paste]. Structure: progress, risks, decisions needed, next week. Keep it under 150 words. Do not soften real risks.
check: Make sure risks are stated plainly.

title: Practice quiz
prompt: Create a 10-question quiz on [topic] at [level] with an answer key and a one-line explanation for each answer. Do not include trick questions. Tell me which topics are best learned from a textbook rather than from you.
check: Check the answer key against your course notes.

title: Study plan
prompt: I have [number] days before [exam]. Topics: [list]. I can study [hours] per day. Make a day-by-day plan with review sessions and a lighter final day.
check: Adjust it to your real energy and schedule.

title: Teach it back
prompt: I will explain [topic] in my own words. Act as a curious beginner: ask one question at a time, point out where I am vague, and do not correct me until I have finished. Then tell me what I got right and what I missed.
check: Compare their feedback with your notes.

title: Lesson outline
prompt: Create a [45]-minute lesson outline on [topic] for [age/level]. Include a starter, a main activity, a check for understanding and a take-home task. List the learning objective first.
check: Check accuracy and age-appropriateness before use.

title: Career practice
prompt: Act as an interviewer for a [role] position. Ask me one question at a time. After each answer, give two strengths and one improvement. After five questions, summarise my pattern.
check: Treat the feedback as practice, not a prediction.

title: Explain this code
prompt:
Explain what the code below does, step by step, in plain English. Then list any assumptions it makes, inputs that could break it, and anything that looks risky. Do not rewrite it.

Code:
[paste code]
check: Read the code yourself and confirm the explanation matches.
tip: Never paste secrets, keys or proprietary code you are not allowed to share.

title: Write tests for a function
prompt:
Write tests for the function below using [framework]. Cover normal cases, edge cases (empty, null, very large) and one failure case. Explain what each test protects against. Do not change the function.

Function:
[paste]
check: Run the tests. A test that passes proves nothing until you have seen it fail.

title: Review a change for risk
prompt:
Review the diff below as a careful reviewer. List: possible bugs, security concerns, missing tests, and anything unclear. Rank by severity. If you are not sure, say so rather than guessing.

Diff:
[paste]
check: Treat it as a second pair of eyes, not the approver. A person decides.

title: Debug from an error
prompt:
Here is an error and the relevant code. Give me the three most likely causes ranked by probability, and for each the quickest check that would confirm or rule it out. Do not propose a fix until I confirm the cause.

Error:
[paste]

Code:
[paste]
check: Run the checks in order. Do not apply a fix you do not understand.
